identity: Writer and film director · Nguyen dynasty · 1914–1996
title: Marguerite Duras's birth chart
metaDescription: Marguerite Duras's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.6° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 13.6° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 13.6° Aries. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Pisces (16.1°), Venus in Aries (26.3°), Mars in Cancer (17.5°): a mind that absorbs before it argues, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts the Sun a sixth of the circle apart from Saturn, 0.0° off exact. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted. Behind it, Venus square Neptune at 0.9°, and Mercury trine Mars at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, five sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aries at 13.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; the Moon in Cancer at 18.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Pisces at 16.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Aries at 26.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Cancer at 17.5° is in fall. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in water, 4 in air, 2 in fire by element, 5 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by modality. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune was retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 18.3°.
